title: Oklo Inc: Meltdown
source_summary: Short-thesis presentation arguing that OKLO's valuation was detached from commercial reality because the company had no revenue, no reactor operating license, no legally binding power-supply contracts, questionable unit economics, large capital needs, prior NRC application rejection, no secured HALEU fuel supply, no smaller-scale or non-nuclear prototype, insider selling, and a stock that had started to decline from its peak.
key_claims: OKLO was a designer of small modular reactors with a market capitalization of almost $19.6B at a $132.77 stock price.
The company had no revenues, no license to operate reactors, and no legally binding contracts to supply power.
Despite being pre-revenue, OKLO traded around a $20B valuation.
The business model depended on aggressive fuel-cost assumptions and large external capital needs not currently secured.
OKLO lacked NRC approval needed to build its first reactor, and the NRC had previously rejected a combined operating and construction license application.
OKLO lacked a long-term HALEU fuel supply in a market with extremely limited domestic commercial supply.
The company was pursuing a commercial license without having built or operated a smaller-scale or non-nuclear prototype first.
SMRs were unlikely to play as large a role in powering AI as the stock price implied.
The stock had fallen almost 24% in late October while the S&P 500 was up almost 3% over the same period.
The Financial Times reported on October 22, 2025 that Oklo executives, including the DeWittes, had sold shares worth about $250M over the prior six months.
The presentation listed P/B above 25x and future revenue based on non-binding agreements.
